summary: Ironclad Supply Co. writes like the crew on its shop floor: blunt, dry and efficient. Specs, repair stories and one-line jokes do the selling; there is no hype, no emoji and no fake urgency.
audience: Tradespeople, ranchers and outdoor people who buy once and buy right, and distrust marketing.

tone_by_email_type.tone: Matter-of-fact: states the discount and the end date, explains why the sale exists, lists a few hero products with specs.
Short origin story (garage in Bend, 2011), sets expectations, one code.
Wry and brief; one line of product proof, offer of help from a real person.
Field story from a real customer, a shop-floor update and a practical tip.
What changed / what didn't, with hard specs and the price.
Contrarian: calls out the noise of big sale events and keeps it short.

signature_phrases: Built for the fourth winter, not the first.
A real person on the shop floor will answer.

mechanics.sentence_length: Very short. Many sentences under 8 words; fragments are normal ("Goatskin. Stitched twice.").
mechanics.person: "We" for the company, "you" for the reader. No named individual sender.
mechanics.capitalization: Title Case subject lines. ALL CAPS only for short section labels inside the body ("THE SHORT LIST").
mechanics.punctuation: Full stops do the work. No exclamation points except in quotes mocking other brands. Em dashes in product lists.
mechanics.formatting: Short paragraphs, ALL CAPS labels, product lists as 'Name — spec. One-liner.', one button.

patterns: Personified gear ("Your Gloves Are Still on the Bench")
examples: Field Day Sale: 30% Off Everything We Make
Your Gloves Are Still on the Bench
The New Ridge Jacket Is Here

patterns: Short fragments that add the proof or the catch
examples: Three days. No gimmicks. Gear that outlasts the sale by about twenty years.
We held them. Not forever, though.

default: one-line opener or ALL CAPS headline
ALL CAPS labelled list with specs

patterns: Two or three words, imperative, Title Case

dos: Lead with specs and real use
Mention the lifetime repair program when relevant
Give exact end dates and times
donts: Write paragraphs longer than three sentences
open_questions: Should P.S. lines ever be used? None of the past emails have one.
